title: On the Origin of the Ly$α$ Damping Wing in Galaxies at $8\le z \le 10$: Explorations using the NINJA Simulations
comment: Submitted to Astronomy & Astrophysics (A&A). Comments are welcome
summary: Ly$α$ damping wing measurements of galaxies at $7\leq z\leq14$ with the JWST provide a powerful probe of the Epoch of Reionization. We combine the large-scale cosmological hydrodynamical NINJA simulations with an idealized ionized-bubble model at z=8 and 10 to quantify the contributions of the intergalactic medium (IGM), circumgalactic medium (CGM), and interstellar medium (ISM) to the observed Ly$α$ damping wing. We generate mock Ly$α$ absorption spectra, and consider three idealized scenarios: (i) galaxies embedded in a uniformly ionized IGM, (ii) galaxies surrounded by HII regions with radii of 0-400 pkpc, and (iii) the same models including Ly$α$ absorption from partially ionized gas within the virial radius. We explore IGM neutral fractions ($x_{\rm HI}$) of 0.1, 0.8, and 1.0, and compare the distribution of inferred HI column densities (NHI) with observations to constrain the sizes of HII regions and $x_{\rm HI}$ of the IGM and gas in and around galaxies. Galaxies are surrounded by over-dense gas extending to $\sim$60-100 pkpc, with its extent increasing with halo mass and showing little evolution between z=8 and 10. The inferred NHI also increases with halo and stellar mass. While the observed incidence of damped Ly$α$ absorption and the median NHI can be reproduced by different combinations of $x_{\rm HI}$ of the IGM and HII region size, models with a uniformly ionized IGM or HII regions larger than $\sim50$ pkpc fail to reproduce the strongest absorbers (NHI>$10^{22}cm^{-2}$). Including partially ionized gas within the virial radius substantially increases the incidence of these absorbers, although the predicted values remain below the observations, suggesting an additional contribution from unresolved gas in stellar birth clouds. The strongest damped Ly$α$ absorbers therefore provide a unique probe of the ionization state of the ISM, CGM, and IGM.

AI.tldr: This paper combines cosmological hydrodynamical NINJA simulations with idealized ionized-bubble models at z=8 and 10 to quantify contributions of IGM, CGM, and ISM to the Lyα damping wing. Mock spectra show that the inferred neutral hydrogen column density increases with halo mass, that models with uniformly ionized IGM or HII regions larger than ~50 pkpc fail to reproduce the strongest absorbers (NHI > 10^22 cm^-2), and that including partially ionized gas within the virial radius increases absorber incidence but still underpredicts observations, implying unresolved gas in stellar birth clouds is needed.
AI.motivation: Lyα damping wing measurements from JWST at z=7-14 provide a powerful probe of the Epoch of Reionization, but interpreting these observations requires disentangling contributions from the IGM, CGM, and ISM to the observed absorption.
AI.method: The authors combine large-scale cosmological hydrodynamical NINJA simulations with an idealized ionized-bubble model at z=8 and 10. They generate mock Lyα absorption spectra under three idealized scenarios: (i) galaxies in uniformly ionized IGM, (ii) galaxies with HII regions of radii 0-400 pkpc, and (iii) models including Lyα absorption from partially ionized gas within the virial radius. They explore IGM neutral fractions of 0.1, 0.8, and 1.0 and compare inferred NHI distributions with observations.
AI.result: Galaxies are surrounded by over-dense gas extending ~60-100 pkpc, with extent increasing with halo mass and little evolution between z=8 and 10. Inferred NHI increases with halo and stellar mass. Observed damped Lyα absorption incidence and median NHI can be reproduced by various combinations of IGM x_HI and HII region size, but uniformly ionized IGM or HII regions larger than ~50 pkpc fail to reproduce the strongest absorbers (NHI > 10^22 cm^-2). Partially ionized virial-radius gas raises absorber incidence but still falls below observations, suggesting additional contribution from unresolved stellar birth cloud gas.
AI.conclusion: The strongest damped Lyα absorbers provide a unique probe of the ionization state of the ISM, CGM, and IGM during the Epoch of Reionization.

title: Emission line formation in scattering dominated media: implications for LRDs
comment: main text: 8 pages, 4 figures. appendices: 8 pages, 2 figures. Submitted to ApJ letters
summary: Recent JWST observations of ``Little Red Dots'' (LRDs) reveal broad and prominent Balmer emission lines. We present a theoretical framework for intrinsic emission line formation and broadening within static, optically thick, scattering-dominated gas envelopes with thermal populations. Using random-walk and diffusion approximations, we derive analytical line profiles for lines forming intrinsically within the scattering medium. We demonstrate that a geometrically thin planar photosphere produces a shallow line profile characterized by a logarithmic plateau and a $v^{-1}$ wing. A radially extended photosphere yields a broken power-law spectrum transitioning from $v^{-α}$ to $v^{-(α+1)}$, with $0 < α< 1$. This is in contrast to a scattering medium external to the line-forming region, which produces an exponential line profile. We show that this broken power-law model can fit the $\mathrm{H}α$ line profiles observed in LRDs. Higher quality spectra may be able to distinguish between intrinsic and extrinsic models for the line broadening in LRDs. In our LTE models, the high contrast between the $\mathrm{H}α$ and continuum flux cannot be explained. Quantitative comparison to LRD spectra requires expanding our models to non-LTE situations.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a theoretical framework for line emission and broadening in static, optically thick, scattering-dominated gas envelopes, deriving analytical line profiles that differ based on whether the line forms intrinsically within the scattering medium or externally. The broken power-law model from radially extended photospheres fits Hα line profiles observed in "Little Red Dots" (LRDs), though LTE models cannot explain the high Hα-to-continuum contrast, requiring non-LTE treatments.
AI.motivation: Recent JWST observations of "Little Red Dots" (LRDs) reveal broad and prominent Balmer emission lines, and the origin of this line broadening is not well understood. A theoretical framework is needed to explain intrinsic line formation and broadening within scattering-dominated gas envelopes.
AI.method: Using random-walk and diffusion approximations, the authors derive analytical line profiles for lines forming intrinsically within static, optically thick, scattering-dominated media with thermal populations. They compare profiles from a thin planar photosphere (logarithmic plateau with v^-1 wing) versus a radially extended photosphere (broken power-law from v^-α to v^-(α+1), with 0<α<1), and contrast these with scattering external to the line-forming region (exponential profile).
AI.result: The broken power-law model successfully fits the Hα line profiles observed in LRDs. Higher quality spectra may distinguish between intrinsic and extrinsic broadening models. However, LTE models cannot explain the high contrast between Hα and continuum flux in LRDs.
AI.conclusion: The intrinsic scattering-dominated line broadening framework provides a viable explanation for LRD Balmer line profiles, but quantitative comparison to LRD spectra requires extending the models from LTE to non-LTE conditions.

title: Luminosity function of quasars at $1.0<z<3.5$ from SDSS and DESI
comment: 16 pages, 6 figures. Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal
summary: We present a study of the evolution of type 1 quasars at $1.0<z<3.5$, covering the peak epoch of quasar activity. The quasar evolution has been extensively explored by a variety of previous works and the derived quasar luminosity functions (QLFs) are not well consistent with each other, presumably due to the complexities introduced by different quasar selection techniques and associated completeness corrections. We use a new strategy to construct QLFs based on a library of all known quasars. We focus on a wide region of $\sim$1700 deg$^2$ and a deep field of $\sim$265 deg$^2$ that have rich spectroscopic data primarily from SDSS and DESI. We then apply traditional color cuts in the rest-frame UV/optical to select quasar candidates and use the quasar library to identify them. Our final sample consists of 62,426 quasars at $1.0<z<3.5$, with a high completeness ($\sim$96%) and a high purity ($\sim$93%) in the color selection. Simple color cuts can potentially minimize selection biases for the study of quasar evolution. We derive binned QLFs and characterize them using a double power-law model. Sample incompleteness and contamination are considered as part of the uncertainties in the calculation. Compared to previous results, our QLFs are slightly higher at the faint end, and also higher at the bright end at $2.5<z<3.5$. The QLFs suggest that the quasar evolution at $1.0 < z < 2.5$ can be well described by the pure luminosity evolution model, while at $2.5 < z < 3.5$, it can be described by either the pure luminosity evolution or the pure density evolution model.

AI.tldr: This study constructs quasar luminosity functions (QLFs) for type 1 quasars at 1.0<z<3.5 using a new strategy based on a library of all known quasars, applying simple rest-frame UV/optical color cuts. The final sample of 62,426 quasars across ~1700 deg² and ~265 deg² fields (primarily SDSS and DESI data) achieves ~96% completeness and ~93% purity. Derived QLFs are slightly higher than previous results at the faint end and at the bright end for 2.5<z<3.5. Quasar evolution at 1.0<z<2.5 is well described by pure luminosity evolution, while 2.5<z<3.5 can be described by either pure luminosity or pure density evolution.
AI.motivation: Previous quasar luminosity function measurements are inconsistent with each other due to complexities in quasar selection techniques and completeness corrections. The authors aim to construct more reliable QLFs by minimizing selection biases through simple color cuts applied to a comprehensive library of known quasars.
AI.method: The authors use a library of all known quasars and apply traditional rest-frame UV/optical color cuts to select quasar candidates across a wide region (~1700 deg²) and a deep field (~265 deg²), drawing primarily from SDSS and DESI spectroscopic data. The final sample comprises 62,426 quasars. Binned QLFs are derived and fit with a double power-law model, with incompleteness and contamination treated as uncertainties.
AI.result: The QLFs constructed show slightly higher values at the faint end compared to previous works, and higher values at the bright end for 2.5<z<3.5. The evolution at 1.0<z<2.5 is consistent with pure luminosity evolution, while at 2.5<z<3.5 both pure luminosity and pure density evolution models can describe the data.
AI.conclusion: The simple color-cut based approach using a quasar library yields reliable QLFs with high completeness (~96%) and purity (~93%), providing improved constraints on quasar evolution across the peak epoch of quasar activity. The results indicate a transition in evolutionary behavior around z~2.5.
